records.title: Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (statute)
records.source_version: As codified, U.S. Code current edition
records.verification_method: Primary-source retrieval (studentprivacy.ed.gov, govinfo CFR annual edition cross-check)
records.source_statement: Conditions federal funding on educational agencies and institutions granting parents and eligible students access to education records and restricting disclosure of personally identifiable information without written consent.
records.reproduction_boundary: Summarised. No statutory text is reproduced in SSLS artifacts; consult the cited source for operative language.
records.notes: Binds educational agencies and institutions, not technology vendors, unless the vendor acts for the institution.

records.title: Family Educational Rights and Privacy (regulation)
records.source_version: CFR annual edition, revised as of 2025-07-01
records.verification_method: govinfo CFR annual-edition PDF plus Cornell LII mirror; live eCFR blocked automated retrieval
records.source_statement: Implements FERPA: defines education records, requires prior written consent for disclosure of personally identifiable information, lists disclosure exceptions including the school-official exception, and establishes inspection and amendment procedures.
records.notes: Currency confirmed against the annual CFR edition rather than the live eCFR currency banner. Recorded as a verification limitation.

records.title: Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment and implementing regulation
records.issuing_body: United States Congress; U.S. Department of Education
records.source_version: CFR annual edition, revised as of 2025-07-01
records.verification_method: govinfo CFR annual-edition PDF plus Cornell LII mirror
records.source_statement: Gives parents rights concerning surveys, analyses and evaluations funded by Department of Education programs that reveal protected categories of information, including notice, consent or opt-out, and inspection of instruments.
records.notes: No recent Federal Register amendment to Part 98 identified in the WP-038 pass. Absence of a found amendment is not proof of none.

records.title: IDEA Part B confidentiality of information
records.source_version: Part 300 as amended; eCFR currency metadata inconsistent at verification
records.verification_method: Cornell LII text; live eCFR page not retrievable
records.source_statement: Directs the Secretary, state educational agencies and local educational agencies to protect the confidentiality of personally identifiable information collected under Part B, consistent with FERPA, and addresses parental consent, access and destruction of information no longer needed.
records.notes: CONFLICTED because eCFR currency metadata for Title 34 was internally inconsistent across pages during verification. Amendment state must be re-verified before any determination relies on it.

records.title: Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (statute)
records.source_statement: Prohibits operators of websites or online services directed to children under 13, or with actual knowledge of collecting personal information from a child under 13, from collecting that information without verifiable parental consent.
records.notes: Citation range varies across FTC pages between 6501-6505 and 6501-6506. Recorded as a citation discrepancy.

records.title: Children's Online Privacy Protection Rule, 2025 amendments
records.verification_method: Direct retrieval and text extraction of the Federal Register PDF
records.source_statement: Amends the COPPA Rule with an effective date of 2025-06-23 and a general compliance date of 2026-04-22, adds a written data retention and deletion policy requirement, and requires separate consent for third-party disclosures for advertising.
records.notes: The 2026-04-22 general compliance date is the nearest dated external trigger tracked by WP-038 and applies only if a child-directed feature exists.

records.title: 603 CMR 23.00: Student Records
records.issuing_body: Massachusetts Board of Elementary and Secondary Education
records.source_version: Most recently amended by the Board 2026-01-27
records.source_statement: Governs Massachusetts student records: assigns rights by student age, defines authorized school personnel to include service-contract personnel with duty-limited access, requires the principal and superintendent to secure records including electronic systems, and sets destruction timelines of sixty years for the transcript and no later than seven years for the temporary record.
records.notes: Obligations are placed on the district. Vendor reach is contractual, not direct regulatory force.

records.title: M.G.L. c. 71 s. 34D — student records regulations
records.source_statement: Directs the board of education to adopt regulations on the maintenance of student records. It is the enabling authority for 603 CMR 23.00.
records.notes: Binds the Board and school committees, not vendors.

records.title: M.G.L. c. 71 ss. 34E, 34F, 34H — related student-record provisions
records.verification_method: s. 34H retrieved directly; ss. 34E and 34F confirmed only as cited authority inside 603 CMR 23.00
records.source_statement: Cited within 603 CMR 23.00 as governing parental inspection rights regardless of student age (s. 34E), retention, duplication and storage of records under school committee control (s. 34F), and noncustodial parent access (s. 34H).
records.notes: Standalone current text of ss. 34E and 34F was not independently retrieved. Recorded UNVERIFIED rather than asserted.

records.title: M.G.L. c. 93H — Security Breaches
records.source_statement: A person or agency that maintains or stores, but does not own or license, personal information about a Massachusetts resident must notify the owner or licensor as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay after discovering a breach.
records.notes: Binds the vendor directly whenever it holds personal information as defined by c. 93H.

records.title: 201 CMR 17.00: Standards for the Protection of Personal Information
records.issuing_body: Massachusetts Office of Consumer Affairs and Business Regulation
records.verification_method: Direct retrieval and text extraction of the official mass.gov PDF
records.source_statement: Applies to all persons that own or license personal information about a Massachusetts resident, requires a written comprehensive information security program with enumerated administrative, technical and physical safeguards, requires oversight of third-party service providers by contract, and sets computer system security requirements including authentication, access control and encryption in transit and on portable devices.
records.reproduction_boundary: Summarised only. Clause-level detail of 17.04 subsections beyond (1)-(3) was not fully enumerated in the WP-038 pass.
records.notes: Personal information here means a name combined with SSN, driver's licence or state ID, or financial account number. This is narrower than FERPA education-record data.

records.title: M.G.L. c. 93I — Dispositions and Destruction of Records
records.source_statement: Requires each agency or person disposing of records containing personal information to meet minimum disposal standards, including redaction, burning, pulverising or shredding of paper records, and addresses disposal performed by a third party.
records.notes: Same narrow personal-information trigger as c. 93H.

records.title: Massachusetts Guidance for Artificial Intelligence in K-12 Education
records.issuing_body: Massachusetts DESE, Office of Educational Technology
records.verification_method: Page and PDF confirmed live; no publication or revision date located in retrieved text
records.source_statement: Sets out principles for ethical AI use as districts adopt and integrate AI, weighing innovation against equity, ethics and system readiness.
records.notes: Non-binding guidance. Date UNVERIFIED, so no as-of date may be cited for it.

records.title: Attorney General Advisory on the Application of Consumer Protection, Civil Rights and Data Privacy Laws to Artificial Intelligence
records.issuing_body: Massachusetts Office of the Attorney General
records.source_statement: States that existing Massachusetts consumer protection, anti-discrimination and data security laws apply to developers, suppliers and users of AI, and creates no new AI-specific statute.
records.notes: Relevant to claim wording about AI capability even before any AI feature exists.

records.title: EOTSS Enterprise Digital Accessibility Policy
records.issuing_body: Massachusetts Executive Office of Technology Services and Security
records.verification_method: Landing page confirmed live; policy text, version and conformance level not retrieved
records.source_statement: An executive-branch enterprise accessibility policy for Massachusetts state agency digital services. Scope as applied to school districts and their vendors was not established.
records.notes: Do not assume WCAG version or district reach. Legal review required before use.

records.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
records.source_statement: WCAG 2.2 is the current W3C Recommendation, retaining conformance levels A, AA and AAA and adding nine success criteria relative to WCAG 2.1 while preserving prior numbering. WCAG 3.0 remains a Working Draft and is not a Recommendation.
records.notes: A voluntary standard. It becomes legally operative only where a regulation incorporates a specific version.

records.title: ADA Title II web and mobile accessibility rule
records.issuing_body: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division
records.citation: 28 CFR Part 35 Subpart H; 89 FR 31320; 91 FR 20902
records.source_version: Final rule 2024-04-24, amended by interim final rule effective 2026-04-20
records.verification_method: govinfo Federal Register text and ada.gov interim final rule PDF
records.source_statement: Requires public entities to make web content and mobile applications readily accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities, conforming to WCAG 2.1 Level AA, subject to listed exceptions and limited defences. The 2026 interim final rule extended compliance to 2027-04-26 for populations of 50,000 or more and 2028-04-26 for smaller populations and special district governments, without changing the technical standard.
records.notes: Regulates public entities including school districts. It does not directly regulate private vendors.

records.title: Section 504 web and mobile accessibility rule (HHS)
records.issuing_body: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office for Civil Rights
records.source_version: Final rule 2024-05-09, amended by interim final rule 2026-05-11
records.verification_method: govinfo Federal Register PDF and HTML text extraction
records.source_statement: Requires recipients of HHS federal financial assistance to conform web content and mobile applications to WCAG 2.1 Level A and Level AA, with compliance dates extended by one year to 2027-05-11 for recipients with fifteen or more employees and 2028-05-10 for smaller recipients.
records.notes: This is the HHS rule. Department of Education Section 504 regulations at 34 CFR Part 104 were not verified in this pass.

records.title: Section 508 ICT standards and guidelines
records.source_statement: Sets accessibility standards for information and communication technology that federal agencies develop, procure, maintain or use, incorporating WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA by reference.
records.notes: Applies to federal agencies and their procurement. It does not apply to Massachusetts school districts.

records.title: EN 301 549 accessibility requirements for ICT products and services
records.source_statement: Harmonises ICT accessibility requirements referencing WCAG success criteria for European public-sector web and procurement obligations. A V4.1.0 revision is in draft and not yet published as a finalised EN.
records.notes: No EU or EEA market entry exists, so this creates no present obligation.

records.title: Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT)
records.source_statement: A blank reporting template published by a trade association. A completed template is an Accessibility Conformance Report and is a vendor self-disclosure. There is no accreditation or certification attached to the template process.
records.notes: No such status as VPAT certified exists.

records.title: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
records.issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology
records.source_statement: A voluntary taxonomy of cybersecurity outcomes organised under six functions. It is neither mandatory nor certifiable.
records.notes: Adoption as an internal organising model does not create or discharge a legal obligation.

records.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, Security and Privacy Controls
records.issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology
section_locators: Control families AC, AU, CM, IA, SC, SI
records.source_statement: A catalogue of security and privacy controls used in the federal Risk Management Framework.
records.notes: Reference only for a pre-pilot vendor with no federal system.

records.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 3, Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information
records.issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology
records.source_statement: Security requirements for protecting controlled unclassified information in nonfederal systems, applied through contract flow-down.
records.notes: Some federal contract clauses still reference Rev. 2. No SSLS federal contract exists.

records.title: CIS Critical Security Controls v8.1
records.source_statement: Eighteen prioritised safeguards against common attack patterns, including a governance function.
records.notes: Voluntary industry practice, not government mandated.

records.title: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Information security management systems
records.source_statement: Requirements for establishing and maintaining an information security management system. Certification is available from accredited certification bodies.
records.notes: Certification requires an accredited body. None has been engaged.

records.title: SOC 2 examination and Trust Services Criteria
records.citation: SSAE No. 18; 2017 Trust Services Criteria with revised points of focus (2022)
records.source_version: TSC 2017 with 2022 revised points of focus
records.source_statement: An attestation examination performed by a licensed CPA firm against the Trust Services Criteria. Type 1 reports on design at a point in time; Type 2 reports on design and operating effectiveness over a period. The output is a report, not a certificate.
records.notes: There is no SOC 2 certified status.

records.title: CycloneDX Bill of Materials specification
records.issuing_body: OWASP CycloneDX working group; Ecma International
records.source_version: ECMA-424 corresponds to v1.6; OWASP latest release v1.7
records.verification_method: Direct retrieval from cyclonedx.org and Ecma announcement
records.source_statement: A machine-readable bill of materials format. ECMA-424 first edition was ratified 2024-06-26 corresponding to CycloneDX 1.6. OWASP released spec v1.7 in October 2025, which is not Ecma ratified. A 2.0 release was announced for later in 2026 and is not released.
records.notes: CONFLICTED because the ratified standard and the latest published spec are different versions. The SSLS pipeline emits CycloneDX and must state which version it emits.

records.title: SPDX specification
records.issuing_body: Linux Foundation SPDX project; ISO/IEC for the 2.2.1 baseline
records.verification_method: Direct retrieval from spdx.github.io and ISO catalogue reference
records.source_statement: An open data model for communicating bill of materials information. The ISO/IEC 5962:2021 designation attaches to SPDX 2.2.1 and has not been confirmed extended to version 3.0.
records.notes: Alternative to CycloneDX. Not currently emitted by the SSLS pipeline.

records.title: Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts (SLSA)
records.verification_method: slsa.dev states v1.2 is current; release date not independently confirmed
records.source_statement: A graded set of build provenance and source integrity requirements for software supply chains.
records.notes: Version date UNVERIFIED. No SLSA level is claimed by SSLS.

records.title: The Minimum Elements for a Software Bill of Materials
records.citation: NTIA SBOM minimum elements report, July 12, 2021
records.source_statement: Defines baseline SBOM data fields including author, timestamp, supplier, component name and version, and dependency relationships.
records.notes: Referenced by federal procurement, not a general private-sector mandate.

records.title: Executive Order 14028, Improving the Nation's Cybersecurity
records.source_version: EO as issued, with NIST guidance updated May 2022
records.source_statement: Directs federal agencies to obtain SBOMs for acquired software and imposes secure-development and self-attestation conditions on software producers selling to the federal government.
records.notes: Procurement condition on federal suppliers, not a general mandate.

records.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0
records.issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology
records.source_statement: Voluntary process guidance for governing, mapping, measuring and managing AI risks. It is neither mandatory nor certifiable.
records.notes: NIST states a revision is in progress. Version 1.0 remains current pending that revision.

records.title: NIST AI RMF Generative AI Profile
records.issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology
records.source_statement: Identifies risks unique to or exacerbated by generative AI and maps suggested voluntary actions to the AI RMF functions.
records.notes: Becomes materially relevant only if a generative AI feature is proposed.

records.title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 AI management system
records.source_statement: Requirements for an AI management system governing responsible AI development and use. Certification is available from accredited bodies.
records.notes: Reference only at present.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Teaching and Learning, and developer guidance
records.issuing_body: U.S. Department of Education, Office of Educational Technology
records.citation: OET AI report (May 2023); Designing for Education with AI: An Essential Guide for Developers (July 2024)
records.source_statement: Non-regulatory recommendations for schools, districts and education technology developers on responsible AI use, stating explicitly that examples are not endorsements and the guidance is not regulatory.
records.notes: Directly addresses developers, which makes it the most relevant AI guidance to SSLS design posture.

records.title: Colorado automated decision-making technology law
records.source_statement: Signed 2026-05-14, substantially scaling back the 2024 Colorado AI Act. Principal provisions take effect 2027-01-01, with certain sections effective on passage. Would impose obligations on developers and deployers of high-risk automated decision-making systems.
records.notes: Watch item only. Not effective, and no Colorado market presence exists.

records.title: 1EdTech OneRoster 1.2
records.source_statement: Standardises exchange of roster, course and grade data between systems. A certification programme exists and conformance is granted only after passing the test suite.
records.notes: Implementing a specification informally is not certified conformance.

records.title: Ed-Fi Data Standard and ODS/API
records.source_statement: A community-governed K-12 data model and API adopted by multiple state education agencies. Conformance is verified through community-run testing rather than a paid certification badge.
records.notes: Most relevant interoperability path for multilingual-learner and special-education program data.

records.title: 1EdTech LTI Advantage, QTI, Caliper, CASE and Common Cartridge
records.citation: LTI 1.3 with NRPS 2.0, AGS 2.0, Deep Linking 2.0; QTI 3.0.1; Caliper 1.2; CASE 1.1; Common Cartridge 1.4
records.verification_method: Direct retrieval from imsglobal.org and 1edtech.org specification pages
records.source_statement: Specification family covering tool launch and grade passback, assessment item exchange, learning analytics events, competency framework exchange and course content packaging. Certification programmes exist for these specifications.
records.notes: Exact release dates for NRPS 2.0, AGS 2.0, Deep Linking 2.0, Caliper 1.2 and Common Cartridge 1.4 were not confirmed. Only versions are recorded.

records.title: Student Data Privacy Consortium National Data Privacy Agreement
records.issuing_body: Access 4 Learning Community, Student Data Privacy Consortium
records.verification_method: Site confirmed live; template version not retrieved
records.source_statement: A multi-state consortium data privacy agreement template that many districts ask vendors to sign. It is a contract template, not law.
records.notes: Obligation arises only on execution of an agreement.

records.title: TEC Student Data Privacy Alliance
records.source_statement: A Massachusetts regional educational collaborative that negotiates data privacy agreements with vendors on behalf of member districts. Its agreements are private contracts, not regulation.
records.notes: Most likely first contractual gate for a Massachusetts pilot.

records.title: M.G.L. c. 30B Uniform Procurement Act
records.verification_method: Not independently retrieved in the WP-038 pass
records.source_statement: Governs local government and school district procurement of goods and services. Content not verified in this pass.
records.notes: Recorded as an UNVERIFIED placeholder so that the gap is visible rather than silent.
